brightport_forenza.m: Yes... maybe I should do that sometime. Take care, $playername.

coin_collector_thief_coins_10.m: Sure. Let's see what you have.

coin_collector_thief_coins_20.m: [The coin collector eagerly examines the pilfered coins, eyes gleaming with fascination.]...

coin_collector_thief_coins_30.m: Ah, these coins tell a tale of clandestine dealings and shadowy alliances.

coin_collector_thief_coins_35.m: These bronze pieces bear the mark of the Lunar Whisper, an infamous thieves' guild that once ruled the underground markets. Legend has it, these coins were minted in secret, their alloy infused with fragments of moonstone to enhance the guild's stealthy endeavors

coin_collector_thief_coins_40.m: These silver coins hold the captivating history of a nomadic people, a seafaring tribe whose exploits were as boundless as the horizon. Born from the hands of skilled minters among the maritime wanderers, these coins tell the tale of the Ocean Nomads, a group of sailors, pirates, and free-spirited adventurers.

coin_collector_thief_coins_45.m: The silver pieces depict a mighty ship sailing under the moonlit sky, capturing the essence of the Ocean Nomads' freedom and unity. Legends speak of these coins being crafted during the tribe's grand gatherings, where sailors from various corners of the seas exchanged not only goods but also these tokens, forging connections that transcended the vastness of the ocean.

coin_collector_thief_coins_50.m:
[The collector pauses, his gaze lingering on the coins.] These pieces are not merely currency; they are artifacts of a hidden past,
a glimpse into the underground world where alliances were forged in secrecy. I'd be willing to make you an offer for these intriguing
tokens of history, should you be interested in parting with them.
r: So you want to buy them all?

coin_collector_thief_coins_55.m: Well, yes. But not all of them. Afterall, who needs 110 of these?
r: OK, so what do you want to buy?

coin_collector_thief_coins_60.m: Well, let's talk price first. You see, the silver coin is worth 11 gold in weight and the bronze is worth 5 gold in weight. But, to a collector they are worth more. Let's make this simple. I will pay you double those values for each coin and I'll take 5 of each.

coin_collector_thief_coins_65.m: 110 gold for the silver and 50 for the bronze coins.
r: Well, something is better than nothing.

coin_collector_troll_coins.m: Ah, these are Enchanted Coins, crafted by ancient wizards who once drew magic from the well's waters. The runes on these coins change patterns, a sign of their magical origin. Such artifacts are rare indeed.
r: What can you tell me about their enchantment?

coin_collector_troll_coins_2.m: The coins hold a faint echo of the well's enchantment. Though their magic is subtle, they carry the essence of the well's power. As a token of my gratitude for bringing these to me, I offer you this rare artifact in exchange for three of these coins. It is imbued with protective magic, much like these coins.
r: Without knowing more about this "rare artifact", I'm afraid that I will have to pass on your offer.
Umm, I guess I can trust you now.

coin_collector_troll_coins_3a.m: Well, if you change your mind, I will be here.

coin_collector_troll_coins_3b.m: For your effort in retrieving these valuable coins, take this rare artifact. It is a relic from the same era as the coins, crafted with similar enchantments. It will serve you well in your journeys, offering protection and a touch of ancient abilities.

forenza_brimhaven_10.m: With an ever growing smile upon his face, Forenza inserts the first key and then the second. He then proceeds to slowly open the chest.

forenza_brimhaven_11.m: Oh, yeah. Let's look in that chest now.

forenza_brimhaven_15.m: Well, go get it and bring me back both the key and the chest.

r: Yes, and I also have the chest. Here, take them. [You give both items to Forenza]
Yes, but I don't have the chest.
What are you talking about? I already gave it to you along with the chest I found on the island.

forenza_korhald_41.m: OK, but don't keep this coin collector waiting too long. I want that coin.

forenza_korhald_cop_0.m: Oh, really?! Let me see them and we can talk more.
r: [You show Forenza the Coin of Prestige and the Shield of the brave]

forenza_korhald_cop_10.m: Hmm...these are indeed interesting. Very interesting in fact.
r: [While trying to hold back the giant smile that you can feel growing upon your face, you ask:] 'Why is that'?

forenza_korhald_cop_20.m: Well, for obvious reasons. Didn't you notice that the shield has the Korhald family crest engraved on its front side? This clearly belonged to Korhald himself. You should keep this item as it could aid you in your adventures.

forenza_korhald_cop_30.m: But this coin you have here really gives my pause, as I never believed the stories about its existence were true.  I don't know much about it, but I do know that it has great value. Can I have it? I will reward you for it of course.
r: Reward?! I always love the sound of that. What are we talking here? {10000} gold? {20000} gold?
Here, take it. I have enough coins.

forenza_korhald_cop_35.m: Oh, how very generous of you to just hand it over for free. I'll tell you what, once you find your way to Brightport, seek out my family. They will reward you for all of your generosity and hard work.

forenza_korhald_cop_40.m:
[While laughing]
Now, now, who do you think I am, Gylew? I don't have that kind of gold. How about {7000} gold?
r: Sounds like a great deal. I'll take it.
Let me think about it. I will be back shortly.

forenza_korhald_cop_50.m: Excellent. Come see me if you ever find any more interesting coins.

forenza_korhald_gylew_not_dead.m: You wimp! Get me my brother's key now.

forenza_waytobrimhaven3_initial_phrase.m: Hey, kid, nice to see you again.
r: It's nice to see you too. Can we talk about the Korhald coins?
Hey. I found the Korhald tomb and it had two items that I think might interest you.
Hey. I found the Korhald tomb and it had two items that I think might interest you.
Inside the Korhald tomb, I found a locked chest. Do you know where I can find its key?
I tried to get Gylew's key, but...
I have not gone back to see Gylew since our last encounter. Why am I wasting time talking to you when the job is not done yet?
Hey. I need to go now and follow this map.
I found these glowing coins in a pit beneath the well in Wexlow Village. They seem magical.
I visited your daughter Florencia in Brightport. She wishes you would come home more often.
We have no more business to discuss. I'll see you later.
I found these glowing coins in a pit beneath the well in Wexlow Village. They seem magical.
I hope that these coins will enable you to make peace with your father. Take care.
[Lie] I have these bronze and silver coins that I "acquired" in a game of chance. I would like to know if you are interested in them.

korhald_chest_examine_10.m: He then begins to feverlessly sift through the coins, transferring each one to his bag. When to his surpirse, he finds something...

korhald_chest_examine_20.m: Look at what I found at the bottom of the chest. A pendant and a map. [Shows item to you]
r: A map? Really? Where does it point to?

korhald_chest_examine_30.m: Well, that is really hard to say. You see [he shows you the map], it is really old and a lot of the landmarks no longer exist in Dhayavar.
r: Yeah, I can see what you mean.

korhald_chest_examine_40.m: But not all hope is lost. You see this map shows the great river that is just right over there [points northeast] behind those trees. Anyone who follows the map going east, should have no problem reaching wherever this map is leading to.

korhald_chest_examine_50.m: Here, take the map and the pendant. If you need me, I'll be here for a little bit longer.

odd_coin_collector_ask_about_locked_ches.m: A locked chest you say? Well, I'm not really sure, but logic tells me to look back in the Laeroth Manor.
r: Oh, come on! I don't want to go back there again.
